summary: The note describes the Dissolution of Czechoslovakia, which took effect on 1 January 1993. The federal state was split peacefully and by self-determination into the Czech Republic and Slovakia. Both successor entities had earlier existed as the Czech Socialist Republic and the Slovak Socialist Republic, created in 1969 under Czechoslovak federalisation.
one_line: The 1993 self-determined split of Czechoslovakia into the Czech Republic and Slovakia, effective 1 January 1993.
key_facts: The Dissolution of Czechoslovakia took effect on 1 January 1993.
The Czech name of the event is Rozdělení Československa.
The Slovak name of the event is Rozdelenie Česko - Slovenska.
The event was a self-determined split of the federal state of Czechoslovakia.
Czechoslovakia was split into the Czech Republic and Slovakia.
The Czech Republic and Slovakia had existed before as the Czech Socialist Republic and the Slovak Socialist Republic.
The Czech Socialist Republic and the Slovak Socialist Republic were created in 1969.
Their creation in 1969 took place within the framework of Czechoslovak federalisation.
